bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your WA Teacher Salary: Hourly to Annual

If you're a teacher in Western Australia, you might be offered an hourly rate or a salary and need to compare them. This guide helps you convert your **wa teacher salary** from hourly to annual using a standard 38-hour week, and shows how tax, super, and fortnightly pay fit in.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time teacher working 38 hours every week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. For example, a rate of $55 per hour gives $55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680 per year. This formula assumes the same hours each week, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances. If you work part-time, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many teachers are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $55/hour example, weekly pay is $55 × 38 = $2,090, so fortnightly is $4,180. This can help you plan bills and savings.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs WA Teacher Salaries

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees receive $33.05 per hour including 25% loading. However, teachers are usually covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. The WA teacher salary is determined by the Department of Education or Catholic Education, often based on classification and years of service. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in WA average $2,227.40 per week (May 2026). This is an average across all occupations, not a median for teachers. Your actual **wa teacher salary** may differ.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you work as a casual teacher, you are entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. For example, a base rate of $50/hour becomes $62.50/hour with loading. Never enter a rate that already includes loading into our [the timesheet](/) – use the base rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time teacher earning $108,680, super would be $13,041.60 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution by your employer.

### Tax Estimates for 2026–27

Resident tax rates for 2026–27: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2%. For a gross annual salary of $108,680, tax would be approximately $24,867 plus Medicare $2,173.60, leaving about $81,639 after tax. This is an estimate – it does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more detail.

### Using Our Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It calculates annual gross, fortnightly pay, super, and estimated tax. It assumes 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. Remember that this is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay or tax.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Further Reading

For more context on pay rates, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page. If you're comparing award rates, visit [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage). For super details, check [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).
